behaviorChanges: A PROJECT MAY NOW DECLARE THE `lean-1` CONTRACT. Four required keys -- `schemaVersion`, `project`, `integrationBranch`, `commands.test` -- plus optional `review`, `security`, `release`, `laneStatus` and `projectRules`. It is validated by a stdlib validator against `methodology/adapter-schema-lean.json`; the 1.x schema is untouched and every existing adapter loads exactly as before.

`tautline slim` IS THE MIGRATION, AND IT NEVER DELETES. Artifacts move rather than vanish, rewritten files are copied to the archive first, an existing archive destination gets a numbered sibling rather than being clobbered, and a config path that escapes the project is ignored rather than followed. Gitignored lane scratch (`.ai-work/`, `.ai-runs/`) is LEFT WHERE IT IS and reported: moving ignored files under `docs/` would un-ignore them and stage whatever was on disk.

THE HOOKS IT REMOVES ARE THE ONES IN `~/.claude/settings.json`. That is where every framework hook writer actually puts them -- the project-local settings file is only ever READ, as a detection fallback -- so a migration scoped to the project directory would have removed nothing a session can feel. A hook is identified by whether its command INVOKES the CLI, word-bounded on both sides, because the framework stamps none of its Claude hooks and `install-hooks` lets an operator override every command string. User-authored hooks are untouched, and a `.before-minervit` hook the installer displaced is reported with the exact `mv` to restore it, never re-armed.

`tautline lane-status` UNDERSTANDS A LEAN ADAPTER. It previously degraded to "lane status could not be computed" against any config failing the 1.x loader's eleven required keys. It remains advisory and still never blocks.

optionalMigrations.description: Declare which workflow is the integration branch's post-merge acceptance suite: `postMergeTier: {workflow: <file-or-name>}` (branch defaults to the integration branch; enforcement defaults to advise). Then `tautline base-health --target .` reports whether the branch you are merging INTO is red. Leave the key absent to opt out entirely.

Set postMergeTier.enforcement=block so `tautline merge` and the pre-push hook REFUSE while the base's post-merge tier is red, released only by the pushing/merging worktree's live claim (`base-red claim:`); merge alone also accepts a recorded --override. Run one release under advise first and read the `base_health_would_refuse` lines before arming.

optionalMigrations.summary: Declare `agents` and `roles` explicitly instead of relying on the legacy vendor-named keys. The compat shim infers them until 1.0.0, and `tautline methodology-status` prints what it inferred and what supersedes each legacy key.

If your builder runs in a harness the framework has not shipped a capability list for, declare it under `runtimeCapabilities` so the enforcement report reflects what that harness actually supplies. An undeclared runtime is reported as zero-capable, which is the safe default rather than the intended path. Whole-entry replacement per runtime: your list REPLACES the shipped one, so a harness that dropped a hook can say so.

optionalMigrations.description: An adopter with no chat tool may now declare `"provider": "none"` on any of the four notify blocks (`iterationReview.delivery`, `milestoneUpdate`, `productChat`, `deploymentNotification`) instead of leaving a Google Chat provider named on a block they never use. Purely declarative today -- a disabled block already performs no I/O -- so there is no reason to touch a working adapter for it. Declaring `none` while the block is `enabled: true` is refused, which is the point: it separates a deliberate opt-out from a broken webhook.

An adopter on Jira may now declare their board: `"provider": "jira"` with `siteUrl`, `projectKey`, optionally `boardId`, and `emailEnv` / `apiTokenEnv` naming the environment variables that hold the account email and API token. The adapter loads, validates and renders. It does NOT yet drive the board: every verb refuses by name until the read and write releases land, so this is worth doing only to have the configuration reviewed early.

An adopter may move a project from the heavyweight profile to the lean one. `slim` archives the project's process artifacts into `docs/archive-prebankruptcy/` (git mv when tracked, so history follows), removes the framework's Claude hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json` and its pre-commit/pre-push git hooks, rewrites `.tautline.json` to `lean-1` preserving project identity, and renders a sub-2KB CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. Nothing is deleted, every rewritten file is backed up first, and running it twice is a no-op. Run it with `--dry-run` first; `--keep-agent-hooks` opts out of touching the agent settings. Steps: docs/reference/lean-migration.md.

requiredMigrations.description: Run this FIRST. The hook's CLI path is baked by whichever install runs install-hooks, so reinstalling from an install that predates 0.49.0 rewrites the hook with the old resolver and reports success.

Then rewrite the hook FROM THE UPDATED CHECKOUT. The command is path-qualified on purpose: an unqualified `tautline` resolves from PATH, which may be the stale install this migration exists to route around, and run there it rewrites the hook with the OLD resolver and reports success. An adopter lane with no framework checkout uses `tautline install-hooks --target .`, which is safe there because the step above already updated the install that `tautline` resolves to. `lane-start` performs the same rewrite.

A board larger than the 5000-item read ceiling now REFUSES rather than silently returning a partial page. On 'board read truncated at N of M', narrow backlogProvider.scopeQuery so the read fits. Boards under the ceiling need no action.
Carried forward from 0.36.0: the declared Python floor is 3.12.
Carried forward from 0.38.0: testEvidence.enforcement defaults to `block`, and a lane with no tautline-test-run/v1 record classifies `missing`.
methodology-status --fail-on-drift requires the fleet-guard-hook PreToolUse entry. Carried forward from 0.17.0; lane-start also repairs it.

requiredMigrations.command: gh auth refresh --hostname github.com -s read:project -s project
requiredMigrations.description: Carried forward from 0.10.3 for lanes updating across it: grant the gh token the GitHub Projects scopes the fail-closed board gates need.

Reinstall hooks so the AskUserQuestion PreToolUse guard is registered: `tautline install-hooks` (settings-managed lanes) or the next `tautline lane-start`, which installs it automatically. Plugin installs pick it up from the refreshed plugin manifest. Until a lane does this the guard is absent, not advisory -- an uninstalled hook reports nothing at all.

ONLY for machines that run an operator launcher created with `--operator-channel`. That launcher now exports a DEDICATED `*_METHODOLOGY_OPERATOR_CHANNEL` signal, and the new checkout reconciliation stands down for it. Until the launcher is regenerated the session does not carry that export, so a session whose checkout sits on another channel's release branch will see `framework_checkout_reconciliation: required` and `methodology-status --fail-on-drift` will exit 2. Regenerate the launcher, or use the one-shot `--allow-non-main` / MINERVIT_METHODOLOGY_ALLOW_NON_MAIN=1 deviation in the meantime. PASS THE LAUNCHER'S OWN `--name`, and keep the `--bin-dir`/`--runtime` you originally used: the default name is the reserved managed-launcher name and the operator install refuses it, so a bare re-run exits before writing and the old launcher never gains the signal. The generic auto-rescue opt-out is deliberately NOT accepted as checkout ownership -- it is a safety setting any managed session may hold, and honouring it would bypass the very contradiction this release exists to catch.

If your framework checkout sits on ANOTHER channel's release branch (channel `stable` with the checkout on `experimental`, or the reverse), resolve it rather than carrying the warning: arm maintainer mode if this machine develops the framework (`tautline maintainer-mode on`), check out the channel's release branch and re-sync, or repoint the channel with `tautline set-framework-channel <channel> --target .`. A one-shot deviation is MINERVIT_METHODOLOGY_ALLOW_NON_MAIN=1. Feature branches and detached HEAD are advisory and need no action.

The pre-push hook gains an unconditional `base-health --boundary pre-push` step. An installed hook without it is reported missing by `git_branch_liveness_hook_state`; `tautline install-hooks --target .` or the next `lane-start` rewrites it. Until then the boundary re-check does not run on that checkout -- absent, not advisory.

Run `tautline install-hooks --target .` (or `lane-start`) in every checkout. The two portable gates reach a machine only when its pre-commit hook is rewritten, and the gap is silent from inside the lane.

rollbackNotes: Reverting is safe for every existing adopter: this release adds a verb and a schema file and changes no existing behavior, so a downgrade simply removes `tautline slim`. A project that has ALREADY been migrated to `lean-1` is the one case to know about -- an older release's loader does not recognise the contract, so its verbs will refuse that project (`lane-status` degrades to UNVERIFIED and still exits 0). Recover it from the project's own git history, or from `docs/archive-prebankruptcy/.tautline.json`, which holds the pre-migration config verbatim. Nothing slim moved was deleted, so a full manual reversal is possible even for a project that was never committed.
